doc.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Mailbox money, Special Payments Fund and Tom Scott
summary: He describes a surprise AT&T commercial check, the union Special Payments Fund and Tom Scott's huge checks.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Do you get unexpected checks in the mail?

Yeah. I don’t make royalties as a producer much anymore, but as a player I remember it was a couple of years ago I get this check for 18 thousand dollars out of the blue and I called I guess I called the union, I said, “What in the world is this for?” And it was something I’d played on they had used for an AT&T commercial, a national commercial. We call it mailbox money. Your royalties and stuff like that. But yeah. Every once in a while you get a nice surprise. Those guys, like Carlton and Tom Scott and all them, every year, you get your scale, whatever you were charging, double scale, triple scale, whatever. And then the union has a thing called the Special Payments Fund for recording musicians. And according to how many sessions you played that year, you’d also get your Special Payments check at the end of the year from the union, and it was not uncommon to see some guy drive up in a new Jaguar or something, after a Special Payments check came in. Because they were big checks. You know who Tom Scott is of course.

Well he was the highest paid musician for a long time in LA. His Special Payments checks were astronomical. And rightfully so. He was phenomenal. He is phenomenal. But he was the highest paid player in LA for a long, long time. By far. Every year they’d say, “An unnamed reed player in Los Angeles again had the biggest Special Payment check.” But everybody knew it was Tom Scott.
